picks.game: New York Mets @ New York Yankees
picks.rationale: The New York Mets are entering this Subway Series opener on a four-game winning streak and have been performing exceptionally well since the trade deadline, boasting a 21-12 record. Their offense is particularly hot, hitting .283 with a .514 slugging percentage over their last six games, contrasting with the Yankees' cooled bats. While starting pitchers Nolan McLean (Mets) and Carlos Rodon (Yankees) have comparable ERAs, the Mets have dominated recent head-to-head matchups, winning 3 of the last 5 and holding a 12-8 all-time advantage. This combination of strong recent form, offensive prowess, and historical edge against their rival makes the Mets a high-value underdog play.

The Baltimore Orioles hold a significant starting pitching advantage with Chris Bassitt (4.96 ERA) taking the mound against Max Scherzer, who carries a concerning 6.03 ERA and has allowed three or more earned runs in three of his last four starts. Baltimore's offense has shown recent capability, scoring nine runs in their last win against Cleveland. Historically, the Orioles have a strong trend as road underdogs against AL opponents following a home win, securing victories in seven of their last eight such games. The slight line movement towards Baltimore further indicates sharp money backing the Orioles in this crucial wild-card race matchup.

The Tampa Bay Rays have a substantial pitching mismatch in their favor, with Drew Rasmussen (14-5, 2.88 ERA, 0.91 WHIP) starting against Houston's Miguel Ullola, a rookie with only 7 innings of MLB relief experience. Rasmussen has been dominant, leading the Rays to nine consecutive wins in his starts, and Tropicana Field is known as a pitcher-friendly park. The Astros' offense has struggled recently, scoring only 38 runs in their last 10 games, which will be further challenged by Rasmussen's command. The line movement towards the Rays, coupled with their strong home record and overall season performance, supports a confident pick on the run line.

picks.game: San Diego Padres @ San Francisco Giants
picks.rationale: The San Francisco Giants offer excellent value at home, primarily due to the strong pitching of Anthony Molina (3-0, 1.88 ERA), whose underlying metrics suggest sustainable improvement, especially in the pitcher-friendly Oracle Park. Padres starter Robbie Ray's 3.39 ERA is misleading, backed by a much higher 4.81 xERA, and he has struggled in recent outings. Furthermore, the Giants' offense has shown better form over the last two weeks with a 105 wRC+ compared to the Padres' 95 wRC+. This significant pitching advantage and recent offensive uptick for the Giants make them a strong moneyline play at plus odds.

The Washington Nationals have a substantial pitching advantage with Cade Cavalli (12-5, 3.12 ERA, 1.18 WHIP) on the mound, who has been in excellent form, allowing just seven earned runs in his last 36 innings. In contrast, Angels starter Yusei Kikuchi (1-5, 4.96 ERA) carries a high 6.10 ERA on the road. Despite the Nationals' recent seven-game losing streak, Cavalli's individual performance provides a strong foundation for this pick. The betting model projects the Nationals to win by 2.7 runs with a 76% win probability, making the +136 odds on the -1.5 spread an attractive value given the clear pitching disparity.

Louisville is a strong FBS team (ranked #24 AP Poll) facing an FCS opponent in Villanova. Villanova has a poor record against FBS teams, going 4-24 since 1985, and is 1-19 against ranked FBS teams. Louisville is coming off a season-opening loss to #9 Ole Miss and will be motivated for a dominant home opener, where head coach Jeff Brohm is 3-0. While there are some injury concerns for Villanova, notably with basketball players mentioned in search results, the football team's specific injury report is less clear, but the overall talent disparity and Louisville's motivation to rebound should lead to a comfortable cover against a team that has a 49-19 record in the FCS over the last six seasons.

picks.game: Norfolk State Spartans vs Virginia Cavaliers
picks.rationale: Virginia enters this game with a significant advantage, having won their last two contests against FCS opponents by a combined score of 89-29. Norfolk State, an FCS team, lost 60-10 to a 5-7 Rutgers team in 2025, indicating their struggles against Power Four opponents. Virginia is dealing with a substantial injury list, with 16 players out and two questionable for their Week 0 game, but many of these are not key starters. The Cavaliers are also undefeated coming off a bye week under Coach Tony Elliott, and this is their first-ever matchup against Norfolk State, providing an opportunity to set a dominant tone.

picks.game: Richmond Spiders vs NC State Wolfpack
picks.rationale: NC State's offense struggled in their season opener, producing only 168 yards in a 34-8 loss to Virginia. Richmond, an FCS team, has started the season 2-0 with solid defensive performances. The last time these teams met in 2013, the combined score was 44 points, going under the 50.5-point total. While NC State is a heavy favorite, their offensive woes combined with Richmond's defensive capability suggest a lower-scoring affair, making the Under a strong play despite Richmond's two Overs to start the year.

picks.game: Rutgers Scarlet Knights vs Boston College Eagles
picks.rationale: The spread for this game has seen movement towards Rutgers, with Boston College opening at -110 and now at -105, while Rutgers moved from -110 to -115. Boston College has a poor recent record against the spread at home, failing to cover in 6 consecutive home games and 9 of their last 10 overall. While Rutgers quarterback Dylan Lonergan left their last game with an injury, AJ Surace is expected to start, and Rutgers still possesses an explosive receiver in KJ Duff. Given Boston College's struggles to cover and the slight line movement towards the underdog, Rutgers covering the 3.5 points is a good value bet.

Missouri will have All-American left tackle Cayden Green returning to play, which is a significant boost for their offense. Kansas, on the other hand, is dealing with key injuries, with starting linebacker Bam Crouch doubtful and wide receiver Cam Pickett a game-time decision. While Missouri's star running back Ahmad Hardy is still out, the return of Green and Kansas's defensive injuries give the Tigers a clear advantage. Missouri is also ranked #23 in the AP Poll, indicating a higher caliber team.
